fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline material state does not reconstruct the single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn model.
The crystallographic loading directions, temperature range, strain-rate range, annealing protocol, and molecular-dynamics controls are omitted.
Twinning-induced plasticity is proposed even though the target result explicitly reports no twinning and identifies Shockley partial dislocations and stacking faults as the deformation mechanism.
The predicted 20% strength-and-ductility improvement and conventional-processing baseline are invented and unrelated to the target comparison.
The cited evidence concerns CoCrFeMnNi or other HEA classes rather than the specified Co-free FeNiCrMn single crystal, so it does not support the quantitative outcome or mechanism.
explanation: The response broadly recognizes that tensile testing and atomistic simulation can investigate FeNiCrMn mechanical behavior, but it does not recover the specific molecular-dynamics study. It misses orientation-dependent loading, thermal softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, rate-dependent dislocation density, vacancy-associated nucleation, and Shockley-partial-generated stacking faults. Its principal mechanism and outcome conflict with the target, while the baseline, boundary, and 15–20% falsification threshold are arbitrary. The proposed experiment measures generic mechanical behavior but cannot discriminate stacking-fault-induced HCP-like regions from a true phase transformation because it lacks CNA/DXA or equivalent structural analysis.
